background.$description:
The page canvas. Neutral is the DEFAULT intention, so it carries no intention word — every other background names its intention (`-brand`, `-danger`).

MOVED gray-2 -> gray-1 on 2026-08-15, which UNDOES a deliberate inversion and is worth understanding before moving it back. This used to sit one step BELOW `background-raised` so cards read as lifted off the page by value alone. It now sits AT gray-1, the same value as `background-raised` and `background-floating` — the orientation Radix actually recommends, canvas lightest with elements stepping darker from it.

WHAT THAT COSTS: a card no longer separates from the page by value at all (contrast 1.00). `esa-card` carries a 1px `--color-border` by default so the outlined and default variants still read — but `esa-card--elevated` has NO border and leans entirely on `--elevation-2`, a 4%-opacity shadow. Check that variant against this before trusting it.

WHAT IT BUYS: the surface ramp now runs in one direction. Canvas gray-1, field gray-2, field hover gray-4, wells gray-3 — every step away from the page is a step darker, instead of the page being darker than the things on it.

background-raised.$description: Cards, panels, anything sitting ON the canvas.

background-floating.$description: Layers that float ABOVE the page — dialogs, dropdown menus, command palettes, popovers. Equal to `background-raised` today; the roles are genuinely different (a theme can separate them once it has an elevation story) so they stay two tokens rather than one.

background-sunken.$description: Wells and inset areas. Step 3 = Radix resting UI-element background. Shares its step with `background-field` but NOT its role — see there for why they are two tokens.

background-field.$description:
The surface of an editable field — text inputs, textareas, selects, comboboxes, date pickers, the checkbox box and the radio circle. Promoted from the tier-3 `--form-bg` on 2026-08-14, which 13 components read: a surface shared by 13 components is an intent, not one component's override.

ONE STEP IN FROM THE CANVAS. It landed on step 3 on 2026-08-14 and moved to step 2 on 2026-08-15, when `background` moved to step 1 — the pairing is what matters, not the absolute step. A field is one step darker than the page it sits on, which is the smallest statement that still says 'you can type here'.

BE HONEST ABOUT THE SEPARATION: gray-2 on gray-1 is contrast 1.03. Step 3 gave 1.11 on a card and 1.08 on the canvas. This is a deliberately quieter, flatter treatment and it puts MORE weight on the border, not less — `--color-border` against this surface is 1.49. If fields start reading as absent rather than quiet, this token is the first thing to move, not the border.

NOT `background-sunken` (gray-3), which is read by 24 components and 10 tier-3 hooks — pill backgrounds, progress tracks, the sidenav rail, card footers. Folding fields into it would rebuild exactly the coupling this token was split out to remove.

Pairs with `background-hover` (gray-4) for the hover surface — a two-step jump from rest, which is deliberate now that rest is so close to the page: 1.16, the clearest state change in the set. Disabled fields take `background-disabled`, which sits at gray-1 so a disabled field flattens INTO the page.

ACCESSIBILITY, recorded not fixed: 1.03 is far below the 3.0 non-text AA threshold, so the border is doing nearly all the work of describing the field's edge. Batched pass.

background-hover.$description: Step 4 = Radix hovered UI-element background. The neutral counterpart to `background-brand-muted-hover`.

background-inverse.$description: Darkest chrome surface — top app bars, dark navigation. Pairs with `content-inverse`. A spoke re-points this to its darkest brand shade.

background-disabled.$description:
Disabled sits at the INTENTION level, not the state level — one disabled definition per property instead of a disabled variant of every intention. That rule is why this did not become `background-field-disabled` when the field surface was promoted on 2026-08-14.

THIS TOKEN DOES NOT PICK ITS OWN STEP — it is pinned one step lighter than `background-field`, and it has moved twice for that reason alone: gray-3 -> gray-2 on 2026-08-14 when the field landed on gray-3, then gray-2 -> gray-1 on 2026-08-15 when the field moved to gray-2. Both times the constraint was the same: a disabled field the same colour as a resting one says nothing.

LIGHTER, NOT DARKER, ON PURPOSE. It now equals the canvas, so a disabled field flattens INTO the page rather than becoming a heavier box — less interactive reads as less present. It also gives the best disabled-text contrast of any candidate step, 3.24 against `content-disabled`. The fill is not carrying this state alone: `border-disabled` softens the edge and `content-disabled` mutes the text at the same time.

The repeated moves are cheap because this role has almost no reach — its only consumer was the old `--form-bg-disabled`, and the eight disabled field surfaces that replaced it.

background-brand.$description: The brand solid fill. Step 9 = Radix solid fill, the canonical interactive fill. Named `brand` rather than `primary` because `primary` is already spoken for one tier down the same word: `content-primary` means the most prominent TEXT, not brand-coloured text.

background-brand-active.$description: The PRESSED fill. Equal to `-hover` in this palette, and briefly deleted for that reason — a mistake. Identical default values do not make two tokens redundant at a layer whose whole job is being re-pointed; `background-raised` and `background-floating` are both gray-1 and stay separate on exactly this reasoning. cb-fish proved it by giving hover and active distinct navy steps. A token earns its slot by naming a real role, not by holding a distinct value. NOTE: 34 of 35 components style `:hover` and only one styles `:active`, so this role is declared but barely delivered — that gap is the real work, not this token.

background-brand-subtle.$description: Step 2 = subtle brand-tinted surface. Section backgrounds, card tints.

background-brand-muted.$description: Step 3 = brand-tinted UI element at rest. Chips, tags, active filter pills.

background-brand-secondary.$description: A second brand fill, for the `secondary` button and badge variants. A VARIANT of brand rather than its own intention — a spoke that wants a genuinely different hue here (cb-fish uses blue) overrides this one token.

background-accent.$description: Decorative highlight, currently only used for map pins and motion demos. Thin surface area — treat a new reader as the first real use.

background-ai.$description: Reserved for AI-generated or AI-assisted UI, so it never collides with brand or status.

background-info-subtle.$description: Step 2 = subtle tinted surface. The usual alert/banner background.

content-primary.$description: Body text and icons. `content` rather than `text` because these are read by icons and SVG strokes too — that was already happening under the old `--color-text-*` names, which made those call sites read wrong.

content-tertiary.$description: A third prominence level. Equal to `-secondary` in the hub's neutral ramp, and briefly deleted for that reason — same mistake as `background-brand-active`. cb-fish runs a four-step grey ramp (900/700/600/500) where this is a distinct step, so the level is real even though this palette does not separate it.

content-muted.$description: The least prominent readable text. Placeholders, timestamps, help text.

content-link.$description: Points at the step-9 SOLID FILL, not step 11. That is inherited, not chosen — it is what `--color-text-link` already resolved to, and this rename was value-neutral by design. `content-brand` (step 11) is the step Radix intends for coloured text on a surface, so this is a candidate to re-point.

content-brand.$description: Brand-coloured TEXT on a surface — link-style buttons, outline button labels. Step 11 is Radix's step for exactly this. Formerly `--color-primary-strong`, a name that read like a bolder fill and got used as one.

content-info.$description: Step 11 = coloured text on a surface.

content-on-brand.$description: Foreground ON the matching solid fill. There is now one of these per intention, because five of them were missing and components hardcoded #fff instead — which silently fails contrast on the bright scales. Grass 9 is not bright, so light text is correct here; override if your brand ramp is.

content-on-brand-secondary.$description: Grass 8 is a bright fill — light text fails contrast, so this is dark. Override when your secondary fill is a dark scale.

content-on-success.$description: Lime is one of Radix's bright scales — its step 9 needs DARK text. Override when your success colour is not a bright scale.

content-on-warning.$description: Yellow is a bright scale — step 9 needs dark text.

border.$description: The default border. Step 7 = Radix element border.

border-subtle.$description: Step 6 = Radix subtle border. Was `--color-border-light`, which described lightness rather than prominence and so did not invert sensibly in a dark theme.

border-strong.$description: Step 8 = Radix stronger border / hovered element border.

border-focus.$description: The focus ring. References the brand SEMANTIC token, not the brand ramp — that is the whole point. It used to be {color.grass.8}, and because spokes re-point semantics and never primitives, the override could not reach it: cb-fish re-pointed the brand to navy and kept Ecology-green focus rings, while its links went navy correctly (those already chained off the semantic). The rule this encodes: a token DERIVED from another intention references that intention's token; only the intention's own definitions may reference a primitive. Moving from step 8 to step 9 also lifts focus-ring contrast from 2.32:1 to 2.95:1 against a raised surface.
